evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches into pricing immediately: 'So now let me go ahead and explain to you how our pricing works and your estimates.' No time-box framing, no dependable-quote promise, no confirmation before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving day confirmed (Saturday October 3rd), storage unit size mentioned (10x45), but no customer name confirmation, no city-to-city route clarity, no independent size verification. Rep jumps to pricing based on incomplete information.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep goes straight into rate explanation without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides typical range ('six to eight hours' for a standard 10x20 unit) but personalizes only minimally — mentions the storage unit configuration (10x45 split into three units at 90% full) but doesn't tie the estimate to customer's stated concerns, prep level, or other context because no concerns were ever discovered.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Fee transparency present: 'the trip fee since...addresses are both outside of the free service zone...it is $190 for the trip fee' and 'no hidden fees of any type. No credit card fees, no deposit, no service fees.' Time framing present: '2.5 hour minimum' and 'prorated in fifteen minute increments.' Full coverage.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep jumps from estimate ('budget around $3,488 to $3,932') directly to 'Do you have questions or clarification about that?' — no 'Does that feel fair?' and no silence wait.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Mentioned with discount framing: 'if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Missing: explicit discount terms (how much, immediate discount start). Partial.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Covered: '$2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Missing: the critical 'no deductible / no fine print' framing that distinguishes this offer. Partial.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar confirmation after presenting the two promises. No explicit close to the Section 5 material.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'will there be anything else Todd that I can help you with today?' — empty throwaway, not genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'would you like me to go ahead and complete your, I mean, secure your schedule for tomorrow' but immediately precedes it with a conditional softener: 'well you know what last two trucks available for tomorrow then yeah, would you like me...' This reads as 'I can do this IF you want' — built-in out. Scored 'with_out.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Never mentioned. No 'your rate is locked in' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms 'two trucks with four movers' and will send email confirmation with 'the details and everything.' Missing: specific arrival window/time, crew size breakdown (which he said but not confirmed back), explicit date and phone reconfirmation, and no notes left for crew about customer concerns (there were no concerns discovered, so none to pass along). Date confirmed (tomorrow, Saturday Oct 3), but not the full set.

top_strength: Strong pricing transparency and fee framing upfront — rep clearly stated the trip fee, no hidden costs, and the 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute increments before the customer had to ask.
coaching_note: Start every call with the quid pro quo framing ('10-15 minutes, walk away with a quote you can depend on') and wait for a yes before diving into pricing — skipping that step misses the chance to set expectations and rushed past the most load-bearing line on the card.
